title: Best Ghostwriters for Books (2026): How to Hire One
description: How to hire a ghostwriter for a book or ebook: what the project should include, how to brief it, rights, what drives the price and red flags.
intro: A ghostwriter writes a book in your name, from your ideas, experience or outline. It is common for business books, memoirs, guides and fiction. Ghostwriting works when the author stays involved and the rights are clear in writing. It goes wrong when the scope is vague, the writer copies or recycles material, or the book is generated with AI without the author knowing. This guide helps you plan a book you can be proud to publish.

faq.a: Normally the author who commissions it, but confirm in writing that you receive all rights and that the writer will not claim credit unless agreed.

faq.q: How involved do I need to be?
faq.a: Quite involved. Expect interviews or calls, reviewing outlines and chapters, and giving feedback. The more of your knowledge and voice you share, the more the book will sound like you.
Ask directly. If you want the book written by a person, or need to follow a publisher's or platform's AI rules, agree on this in writing.

faq.q: How long does a book take?
faq.a: It depends on length, research and your availability. A full-length book usually takes months, not weeks.
Sometimes. Ghostwriting and editing are different skills. Plan for an edit and proofread before publishing.
